title: Framework completed pullback scalar comparison commutes with shifts
statement:
Fix the global datum $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, and an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. Let $E\subset L\subset\Omega$ be finite extensions of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation rings $\mathcal O_E,\mathcal O_L$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. For $W=X,Y$, use the derived-complete integral constructible category $\mathcal C_F(W)=D^b_c(W,\mathcal O_F)$ for $F=E,L$ [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]. Write $F_{f,F}=Lf_F^*$ for the completed pullback of [def-pur-integral-derived-operations], and $T_W=T_{L/E,W}$ for the completed strict-tower scalar extension of [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension].

Let $\theta_{f,E,L}:T_XF_{f,E}\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{f,L}T_Y$ be the pullback scalar comparison of [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension], with the specified whole-tower realization normalization of [lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization]. Give $F_{f,F}$ and $T_W$ their canonical integer shift comparisons induced by shifting the K-flat representative and its entire quotient tower in their defining derived-limit constructions. For a functor $A$ write $\chi_{A,K,m}:A(K[m])\xrightarrow{\sim}(AK)[m]$ for this comparison; for a composite $AB$ use $\chi_{AB,K,m}=\chi_{A,BK,m}\circ A(\chi_{B,K,m})$ [def-weil-triangulated-category]. Then, for every $K\in\mathcal C_E(Y)$ and $m\in\mathbf Z$, the following equality holds in the derived category:
$$
\chi_{F_{f,L}T_Y,K,m}\circ\theta_{f,E,L,K[m]}
=(\theta_{f,E,L,K})[m]\circ\chi_{T_XF_{f,E},K,m}.
$$
Its inverse satisfies the corresponding reversed equation. The same equations hold after raw rationalization [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], with the rationalized comparisons used in the prescribed pullback of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom].

proof.text: Equip the actual total limits with their right-derived shifts, the supplied reduction functors with adjoint-mate shifts, exact sequence pullbacks with their termwise derived shifts, and sequence scalar change with its universal-counit shift. These choices are fixed independently of lambda and mu.

The normalized completed pullback realization and completed scalar realization commute with these fixed shifts, by the two realization lemmas. Reduction of either realization followed by the actual adjunction counit therefore commutes with shifts: the counit has the adjoint-mate shift equation. Whisker and compose these maps to obtain the natural transformation lambda from completed scalar after pullback to the common strict-system realization. It commutes with shifts.

The generator-normalized sequence scalar/pullback comparison commutes with the independently fixed sequence shifts. Whisker its inverse with reduction and total limit and compose it with pullback realization and the reduced scalar counit. This gives the natural transformation mu to precisely the same common strict-system realization, commuting with the same shift.

On constructible inputs lambda and mu are exactly the integralComparisonLambda and integralComparisonMu isomorphisms. Their defining scalar comparison a satisfies a followed by mu equals lambda, at both K and K[m]. Precompose the natural transformation shift equations by the inclusion comparison K[m].obj → K.obj[m]. Naturality gives the same common realization shift on the right. Postcompose the desired a square by shifted mu, substitute the two equations and a followed by mu equals lambda, and cancel this invertible shifted map. The output constructible inclusion comparison cancels from both sides; its naturality is exactly the inserted inverse comparison in SourceShift and TargetShift.

Precompose the forward square by a at K[m] to deduce the inverse square using both inverse identities. Apply raw rationalization to the two integral equations; its preservation of composition yields the two rational equations. All comparisons and the target statement are unchanged.
